To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the refraction of a plane wave propagating through the layer with a high sound speed vertical gradient results in the appearance of the pressure max/min and the vertical velocity max/min in the vertical direction within the layer.

the spatial structure of the acoustic field in a liquid layer with a high sound speed profile is characterized by alternating pressure and velocity maxima and minims, and that the number of these alternating maxima and minis increases with increasing frequency.

the refraction of acoustic waves propagating through a gradient layer in a fluid near a pressure-release boundary is characterized by strong maxima in the pressure and the particle velocity near the cut-on frequency of the acoustic duct, and that these maxima are caused by the interference of the incident and reflected waves.

the acoustic wave propagation in an acoustic duct near a pressure-release boundary.
the refraction of a plane acoustic wave propagat-ing through a layer with a high sound speed gra-dient.
the acoustic wave propagation in an inhomogeneous liquid layer with a high sound speed profile.

the acoustic wave field within the layer is strongly affected by the high sound speed gradient.
the spatial structure of the acoustic wave near the surface is formed in the vicinity of the acoustic duct cut-ons.

a plane wave incident on a high sound speed layer near a pressure-release boundary is refracted and reflected in such a manner that the vertical velocity of the acoustic wave is enhanced near the surface and the pressure is enhanced near the bottom of the layer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spatial structure of the acoustic field in the vicinity of the cut-on frequencies is very complicated.
the acoustic wave propagating near a pressure-release boundary in the layer with the sound speed gradient can be described as the sum of two plane waves.

the refraction of acoustic waves propagating through a liquid near a free surface with a high sound speed vertical gradient can be described by two distinct processes: (i) the refraction of a plane wave propagating through an acoustic duct with a cut-on frequency, and (ii) the refraction and scattering of a plane wave at a pressure-release boundary.

a high sound speed layer with a high gradient near a pressure-release boundary is a good candidate for the development of a high-resolution acoustic lens.
the acoustic wave propagating near a pressure-release boundary in a liquid layer with a high sound speed profile has a distinct spatial structure.
